Validate new data against a "stabl_predictor" schema

Source: R/finalize.R
validate_newdata_schema.Rd

Checks newdata against the column schema recorded at stabl_finalize() time and returns the required columns as a numeric matrix in training order. Column names must be present, non-empty and unique; missing or duplicated required columns are always an error; non-numeric columns are an error; extra columns are an error unless extra_columns = "drop" is given explicitly.

Usage

validate_newdata_schema(object, newdata, extra_columns = c("error", "drop"))

Arguments

object

A "stabl_predictor" from stabl_finalize().

newdata

A data frame or numeric matrix with column names.

extra_columns

Policy for columns not required by the model: "error" (default) or "drop" (explicit opt-in; the extra columns are discarded).

Value

A numeric matrix with exactly the required columns in training order. For an intercept-only model (empty selected panel, no preprocessing) the matrix has zero columns and nrow(newdata) rows: the model ignores all feature columns.

Examples

set.seed(2L)
ids <- paste0("s", 1:60)
x <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 6), 60, 6,
            dimnames = list(ids, paste0("f", 1:6)))
y <- setNames(2 * x[, 1] - x[, 2] + rnorm(60), ids)
fit <- stabl_fit(x, y, lambda_grid = data.frame(lambda = c(0.3, 0.2, 0.1)),
                 family = "gaussian", n_bootstraps = 20L, random_state = 2L)
final <- stabl_finalize(fit, x, y, random_state = 2L)
req <- final$required_columns
stablr:::validate_newdata_schema(final, x[1:3, rev(req)])  # order does not matter
#>            f1         f2
#> s1 -0.8969145 -1.7882422
#> s2  0.1848492  2.0312425
#> s3  1.5878453 -0.7031443
